issues.body: Step C still says to run `python3 scripts/ledger-invariant.py` against a fresh checkout of the rewritten branch. The shipped CLI requires a positional checkout root unless `--self-test` is used, so the literal command exits in argparse without checking the tree. The rewritten `ledger` checkout is also intentionally data-only and therefore has no `scripts/ledger-invariant.py` to execute. The later contents-API and parser checks do not perform this separately prescribed allowlist/tree-shape validation. This is the same major defect recorded in round 4.
issues.fix_hint: Name two distinct checkouts and provide an exact executable command: invoke `scripts/ledger-invariant.py` from a trusted registry code checkout pinned to a specified reviewed SHA, and pass the fresh rewritten-ledger checkout as its positional root, for example `python3 <registry-code-checkout>/scripts/ledger-invariant.py <rewritten-ledger-checkout>`. Keep the code source and validation target explicit and distinct.
issues.title: The ledger-invariant post-check still cannot run as written

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major finding remains materially unchanged. Step C still prescribes `python3 scripts/ledger-invariant.py` against a fresh rewritten-ledger checkout, but the literal command has no required root argument and therefore exits through argparse without validating anything. In addition, the rewritten branch is explicitly data-only, so it does not contain the referenced script. The subsequent contents-API and schema checks validate tip content but do not execute the separately required Git tree allowlist check. The maintenance runbook remains non-executable as written at a fail-closed post-rewrite gate.
